fun_highlights: The callback system genuinely earns its keep. When Ren Salvedi (Dynasty 6, gen 2) finds at age 49 the exact book he kept at age 11, or when Edmund Ashby (Dynasty 2, gen 2) stops for the rough sleeper at age 57 to make up for the childhood look-away at age 10, the read-back lands with the weight the genre promises. These are the moments a life-sim lives or dies on, and they work.

The vocation arcs create meaningfully different life shapes. A soldier's life (Linnea Okonkwo, Cyrus Ashby, Theda Quint) runs through 'a_soldier_service', 'm_soldier_ghost', and 'e_soldier_old' in a way that genuinely differs from a scholar's arc ('cb_study_pays', 'm_scholar_legacy') or a maker's ('a_maker_shop', 'm_maker_masterwork', 'e_maker_handoff'). Across 15 dynasties you can feel the structural difference.

The era layer adds meaningful macro-texture. Dynasty 6 (Ren, in a war era) earns 'w_war_loss' and the soldier-calling in a way that differs from Dynasty 14's fat-years founder. The era-coloured text variants on 'y_calling' and 'a_marry' mean the same beat reads differently each generation. Dynasty 11 (plague era) gets the 'Tend them. Stay close' moment that no other dynasty touches.

The dynasty accumulation layer has genuine feel. Mottos crystallizing ('Better a short blaze than a long smoke' for House Salvedi, 'We do not save ourselves for later' for House Okonkwo) after 3-4 generations of matching choices feels earned, not cosmetic. The heirloom chain of 'a book too hard for a child's hands' passing through Dynasties 6, 8, 11, 12, 13 gives a tactile thread across many lives. Inheritance disputes, the family shadow card, and the patronage moment gate real content at high standing.

The prose quality is consistently high and occasionally excellent. Lines like 'Kept the question for evenings and the paid work for days, and made, between them, a sufficient life' (appearing in Dynasties 2, 6, 14) and the late-love framings ('across a table, across a season, across the better part of a life — someone') land with real compression. The observation pool for spirit/mind/means stats adds ambient texture without demanding choices.

The drifter arc (vocation='adrift') is a genuine fifth life-shape. Calla Okonkwo (Dynasty 11, gen 5) runs 'a_adrift_work', 'm_adrift_reckon', and 'e_adrift_old' and reads as a fundamentally different life from every soldier or scholar in the set. The late line 'Tallied, at the last, what a single chosen road might have built — the mastery, the belonging, the name — and felt the absence of it plainly, and let it be' is the genre at its best.
staleness: The 'look away from a lonely child / later encounter a rough sleeper' two-beat sequence fires in a striking number of lives and generates near-identical prose strings across the transcripts. The exact sentence 'Looked away from a lonely child, and the small shame of it stayed' appears verbatim at: Carys Brandt age 12, Iris Brandt age 12 (different dynasty), Niall Marchetti age 12, Annika Okonkwo age 9, Yara Okonkwo's transcript (via the friend card variant). The cb_lookaway payoff ('Looked away a second time, and knew, now, exactly what it cost') then follows in Iris (age 61), Niall (age 51), Annika (age 55). Reading all 15 dynasties in sequence, this arc feels like standard issue.

Body-decline observations recur verbatim with very high frequency. 'Some mornings the body answers the bell late, and grumbling', 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them', 'The body has begun sending its small bills', 'Mornings take longer to arrive in the body than they once did' — these appear in almost every long life, and multiple instances appear within the same dynasty because the engine's observe() pool fires these as stat-triggered one-time lines, but across a session of 15 dynasties they become a wallpaper. Within Dynasties 1-8 alone I count over 20 distinct elder body-complaint lines appearing, most of them familiar from a prior dynasty.

The marriage beat, while well-written, produces a structural predictability: 'love arrives → years of courtship → marriage proposition'. The actual marriage prose is well-varied ('Nobody made a speech; the years that followed were the speech'; 'Married with borrowed rings and no money and a great deal of nerve'), but the three-stage beat itself and the clustered placement (love ~20s, marriage ~30s) recurs in the majority of lives that reach adulthood. In Dynasty 2, Dynasties 6, 8, 11, 12, 14, and 15, every generation that survives to adulthood follows this exact arc.

The 'gave away all knowledge / taught the young' beat and epitaph cluster dominates. The epitaph 'Gave away everything they knew, and so kept it' (and its exact variants) appears in the closing lines of: Tobias Ashby, Lazlo Bjornsen, Junia Calloway (verbatim despite the cross-session RECENT_LINES dedup), Niall Marchetti. The dynasty.js dedup logic tracks these, but with 15 dynasties in a row the 'teacher' cluster visibly recurs. The underlying card 'm_scholar_legacy' also generates near-identical resolution lines ('Gave away everything they knew, freely and to anyone who'd take it') in multiple mid-session dynasties.

The calling card ('y_calling') generates four possible vocations but in practice scholar and maker dominate the transcripts. Across 15 dynasties: soldier appears in roughly 7 lives, scholar in ~8, maker in ~7, wanderer in ~4, adrift in ~2. The structural variety is there, but a long session produces multiple consecutive scholar lives (Dynasties 2, 4, 6 gen 4, 11 gen 4, 13, 14) where 'cb_study_pays' and 'm_scholar_legacy' fire in near-identical order and the lines 'the wager of those lean studying years came in at last, and handsomely' and 'kept what they knew close and well-defended, the way a thing dearly bought is kept' start to feel like parts of a template.

The founding moment 's_from_nothing' ('There is nothing behind them — no name that means a thing') fires very frequently, nearly every founder and many second-generation heirs trigger it, generating the same two paired outcomes ('Build, brick by brick' / 'Find others to climb with') and their associated lines. By Dynasty 8 or 9 in a session these feel like a mandatory stop on every low-seat life rather than a characterful moment.

improvements.what: Add a third branch to the 'cb_lookaway' callback — something that sidesteps the rough-sleeper frame entirely for lives where the original look-away happened in a different context (e.g. the 'c_friend' route vs. the 'c_friend' refusal). The current callback always uses the same rough-sleeper prompt regardless of which look-away was the origin, making the payoff feel mechanical. Gate alternate payoff prompts on which specific memory fired.
improvements.why: The look-away / rough-sleeper arc appears verbatim in at least 5 of the 15 dynasties. It is the single most visible repetition in the transcript set. A differentiated payoff based on memory origin would make each instance feel particular rather than templated.

improvements.what: Thin the 'observe()' body-decline pool by raising the age floor on its most common lines and adding a 'already fired this cluster recently' cross-dynasty cooldown (analogous to RECENT_CLUSTERS in dynasty.js). Currently the obs lines fire once per life, but a session of 15 dynasties means each pool line can appear 15 times. A global session-level dedup (like RECENT_LINES for epitaphs) applied to the top-3 most-fired observe keys would cut visible repetition.
improvements.why: Body-complaint observations currently constitute the dominant ambient prose in elder sections across the full transcript. They are well-written individually but arrive so predictably that they become background noise. Reducing their frequency per session would make the ones that do land feel more earned.

improvements.what: Break up the three-stage love arc (y_love1 → a_marry → a_child) by adding a genuine alternative track for lives where the love card fires but marriage is declined — specifically a 'committed partnership without marriage' path that sets a different flag and produces distinct mid-life content. Currently declining marriage just decays the bond; the life then often has no love-arc content at all. A 'chose not to marry but kept building' path would give the refusal real downstream consequence.
improvements.why: The marriage beat's structural predictability is the second most visible template in the transcripts. Almost every adult life follows the same three-step domestic arc. A genuine alternative shape for non-marrying couples would make 'Not yet. Maybe never' feel like a real life-choice rather than a failure state.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 new calling-specific midlife moments for the scholar arc that are not about the knowledge-give-or-guard fork. Currently a scholar's midlife is 'a_scholar_question' (chase the question or take paid work) + 'm_scholar_legacy' (give away or guard). A third branch — perhaps a moment where the scholar's conclusions are publicly challenged or proved wrong, forcing a reckoning with intellectual pride — would break the scholar template and differentiate scholarly dynasties from one another.
improvements.why: Scholar lives dominate the transcript and their midlife arc is among the most predictable. 'cb_study_pays' followed by 'm_scholar_legacy' appears in near-identical order in Dynasties 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, and 14. A third structural beat with no 'correct' answer would add the variance the vocation currently lacks.

improvements.what: Gate 's_from_nothing' on generation 1 or seat 0 only (not seat 1), and replace it for seat-1 heirs with a distinct 'the house is struggling but not empty-handed' moment that acknowledges the inherited-but-thin starting position rather than treating it as a clean-slate founding moment. Currently collateral heirs at seat 1 and seat 0 founders get identical prompts about 'nothing behind them', which is narratively incorrect for a second-generation heir of a house with a struggling rented room.
improvements.why: The founding 's_from_nothing' card fires in the majority of low-seat lives regardless of generation, making Dynasty 3 gen 1 and Dynasty 8 gen 2 feel structurally identical in a way the dynasty layer is supposed to prevent. Differentiating the 'nothing' moment by actual generation and house standing would sharpen the generational contrast.

verdict: A Life is a genuine, thoughtful entry in the genre with real strengths: the callback system, the vocation arcs, the era layer, and the dynasty accumulation all work and occasionally produce the pull-to-play-another-life feeling the format demands. At a single dynasty it plays closer to a 7.5. The problem is session-length: across 15 dynasties the staleness the engine is actively fighting — body-complaint prose, the look-away/rough-sleeper arc, the scholar template, the three-stage domestic arc, the 's_from_nothing' beat — becomes visible and cumulative in a way the current dedup mechanisms don't fully contain. A genre veteran playing 4-5 dynasties in a row will feel the template underneath the variation. The game is a strong foundation that needs its highest-frequency beats either thinned or replaced with more contextually differentiated variants before it reaches the 'one more dynasty' compulsion of the genre's best examples.
